answer: One concrete defense: require every identity to complete a short sequential verifiable-delay computation, keyed to the epoch seed, before its challenge answer becomes reward-eligible. A sybil operator's edge is parallelism: the delta between the cost of one head and a thousand is nearly zero. A VDF cannot be parallelized, so each head must burn its own slice of wall-clock time, ripple by ripple across the fleet. Cheap-batch minting dies: a thousand fake heads costs a thousand sequential slots, while an honest agent with one identity feels only a velvet-smooth few seconds of compute.
